findings.F1: The book's loss comes from its short side. Its 313 short trades lost 12.0 % on average after fees (median −11.7 %), while its 106 long trades gained 13.6 % (median +2.65 %). Bar by bar, the 2,709 short position-bars gave −0.081 % each (−2.20 summed) and the 962 long position-bars gave +0.228 % each (+2.19 summed). The two sides cancel, which matches the verdict's normal drift of −1.99 % per case in the position's direction.
findings.F2: Inside the choppy-calm profile, the week's raw multiple does not predict the coin-demeaned forward return at any horizon. With day-clustered errors, the t is −0.06 over 3 days (342 cases, 156 days) and 0.62 over 7 days (148 cases, 64 days). Unclustered, it is 1.81 over 14 days (71 cases) and 1.87 over 28 days (30 cases). This agrees with step 5's slope t of −0.04 on 188 grid cases.
findings.F3: Outside the profile, the weekly multiple's link to the next 3 days looks strong unclustered (t 4.01, 2,182 cases) but falls to t 1.74 once the cases of one day are taken together (399 days). It stays under 2 in every trend split: rising t 1.18, falling t 1.15, choppy t 1.58 on 41 cases. Its yearly slopes are all positive (2018 to 2021: 0.061, 0.025, 0.066, 0.019), but each has a t of 0.8 or less.
findings.F4: Weekday effects shrink once one day's coins count as one piece of evidence. Friday and Saturday show coin-demeaned means of +0.37 % and +0.44 % (t 1.20 and 1.71, about 207 days each), against t 3.42 and 4.51 when every coin-day is counted. The Friday-Saturday edge over the other days is positive in each year from 2018 to 2021, but it is small in 2021 (+0.27 % against +0.21 %).
findings.F5: The daily-move angles are thin or flip sign across horizons, so none can be told from chance across this many looks.

no_ideas: Across the forecast, the positions and trades, the trends and the bars (weekly and daily scaled moves, volatility, weekday, horizons from 3 to 28 days, by year), no pattern keeps a day-clustered t of 2 or more. The book's loss is the short side paying the coins' upward drift (F1), and the one sizeable daily pattern is a rebound the map already holds (F5).
